subject: How to make model work faster

messages.author: 47847628200bd730
messages.subject: How to make model work faster
parts:
Hello everyone! 

I`m just wondering if it`s possible to make my model work faster?

predictions_of_bayesian_hierarchical_multi_logit <- "
data {
int N;                           // number of individuals
int<lower=2> K;                  // number of alternatives
int<lower=1> D;                  // number of individual predictors
int<lower=1> C;                  // number of cards for train sample
int<lower=1> C_tilde;            // number of cards for test sample
int<lower=1> L;                  // number of groups
int<lower=1,upper=L> ll[N];      // group for induvidual 
matrix[K,D] X[N, C];             // individual predictors
matrix[K,D] X_tilde[N, C_tilde]; // individual predictors for test sample
int<lower=1,upper=5> y[N, C];    // outcomes 
}
parameters {
vector[D] mu;                 // mean vector
corr_matrix[D] Omega;         // prior correlation
vector<lower=0>[D] tau;       // prior scale
real<lower=0> sigma[D];       // prediction error scale
vector[D] beta[L];            // individual coefficients 
}
model {
tau ~ cauchy(0, 2.5);
Omega ~ lkj_corr(2);
for (d in 1:D) {
mu[d] ~ normal(0, 5);
for (l in 1:L)
beta[l] ~ multi_normal(mu, quad_form_diag(Omega, tau));
}
for (n in 1:N)
for (c in 1:C)
y[n, c] ~ categorical_logit(X[n, c]*beta[ll[n]]);
}
generated quantities {
    int<lower=1,upper=5> y_tilde[N, C_tilde];
    for (n in 1:N)
    for (c in 1:C_tilde)
        y_tilde[n, c] = categorical_rng(softmax(X_tilde[n, c]*beta[ll[n]]));
}
"



Thanks in advance! :)

messages.author: 3d7541308bd2e290
messages.subject: Re: How to make model work faster
parts: Is this adapted from the example in 8.13 of the manual? I'm not really familiar with the modeling here, but off hand it looks like:

for (l in 1:L)
  beta[l] ~ multi_normal(mu, quad_form_diag(Omega, tau));
}

In that loop you're doing L quad_form_diags. Can you do a similar trick as is in 8.13 and do:
{
  matrix[K, K] Sigma_beta;
  Sigma_beta = quad_form_diag(Omega, tau);
for (l in 1:L)

beta[l] ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma_beta);
  }
}

Look through the rest of that section and see about the other tips. Maybe they apply. I think you should be able to do a Cholesky something here too, and that multi_normal could probably just be vectorized (look for multi_normal_cholesky, cholesky_decompose and examples of vectorization in the manual).

And as always, it might not be a computational issue. If there are identifiability issues n' such in the model it might just take a long time for the sampler to explore things. If you got an inference to finish, check out your posterior samples and see if there are big correlations between parameters.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to make model work faster
parts:
Two things:

1. Use a Cholesky factor parameterization. There's an example
in the regression chapter of the manual on how to scale.

2. Vectorize multi_normal_cholesky. (There's no way to vectorize
that categorical logit because the parameter is customized for each
outcome.) You can also vectorize the mu sampling as just mu ~ normal(0, 5);

4. Indent the code so it's readable.

The key is to not repeat expensive operations like factoring
a matrix.

- Bob
